query: Rings on Still Water The lake is flat calm, and still rings spread from its middle, slow and even, like the ripples from a bell that nobody hears. A heron on the shallows lifts its head at each one. Count the rings Seven, then a pause, then seven. The heron counts them too, you'd swear. You walk back up the lawn with the number stuck in your head. Skim a stone across them Your stone skips four times and sinks in the middle of a ring. For a moment the rings stop. Then they start again, patient as anything.
